headline: Recommended $2,495,000 for Board of Education and $59,800 for timeclocks; approved BSN Sports uniform bid waiver and Avila software bid waiver.
summary: Approved a $26,589 bid waiver to BSN Sports for high school uniforms and a bid waiver to Avila for grant management software. Recommended budget transfers and appropriations, including $2,495,000 for the Board of Education and $991,338 for the Supplemental Municipal Assistance Grant. Placed the Insurance Committee report on file.
decisions: Recommended approval of the consent agenda, including routine budget transfers and appropriations, by voice vote with no opposition
Recommended a $5,849 transfer from the General Fund Contingency Account and an $11,698 additional appropriation for the 2025 Bulletproof Vest Partnership Program, by voice vote with no opposition
Recommended transfers totaling $2,475,081 within the General Fund to close out fiscal year 2025-2026, by voice vote with no opposition
Recommended carryovers totaling $1,253,585 within the General Fund from fiscal year 2025-2026 to fiscal year 2026-2027, by voice vote with no opposition
Recommended carryovers totaling $7,855 within the Community Development Block Grant Fund from fiscal year 2025-2026 to fiscal year 2026-2027
Approved a bid waiver to Varsity Brands Holding (BSN Sports) for $26,589 in high school uniforms, by voice vote with no opposition
Recommended a $2,495,000 additional appropriation within the General Fund for the Board of Education

Approved a $4,850 transfer from the General Fund Contingency account and appointed Fiducient as Discretionary Investment Manager of the City’s 457 Deferred Compensation Program, by voice vote with no opposition
Recommended a $59,800 transfer from the EBSF Contingency account to purchase timeclocks
Recommended a $991,338 additional appropriation within the General Fund for the Supplemental Municipal Assistance Grant
Approved a bid waiver to Avila for grant management software for the ECD, by voice vote with no opposition
Accepted the Insurance Committee report of July 30, 2026 and placed it on file, by voice vote with no opposition

6. Board of Education:   
a. Budget Update 
 
Jodi Bond gave the report of the Board of Education as of August 5, 2026. $61,801 remains 
encumbered, pending receipt of a few late invoices. She does anticipate this deficit to shrink a bit 
further. The Special Education deficit is ($3,150,151), with $5,959 still encumbered. 
Private & Public (outplaced) Tuitions, Professional Services, and Sub Paras are the main drivers of 
this deficit. Thanks to the DRIP and SEED Grants, and bringing some students back in 
house additional savings were generated in the general fund, to reduce the originally anticipated 
deficit. 
 
Pending May and June Federal and State reimbursement, the 2026 Cafe snapshot reflects a surplus of 
$125,731. This surplus will be fully expended in FY 27. 39,899 breakfasts, 83,727 lunches, and 529 
snacks in were served in June. 
 
Pending July Federal and State reimbursement, the 2027 Cafe snapshot reflects a surplus of $166,156. 
This surplus will be fully expended in FY 27. 10,105 breakfasts and 11,393 lunches were served in 
July. 
 
Chairman Maikowski questioned the plan moving forward for the Cafeteria and proposed deficit. 
Mayor Zoppo Sassu stated discussions have already begun regarding changes that need to be made in 
the program in general. 
 
As of August 1, 2026, 1,722 of the 7,646 enrolled Bristol students are identified as requiring Special 
Education programming. This enrollment reflects 22.52% of the total BPS student population. 
As of August l, 121 students with disabilities required out-of-district placements at private special 
education school programs. There were 89 students requiring special education programming services 
at other public out-of-district schools, including magnet schools. 
 
During the month of July 2026 46% (31 of 68) of the newly registered students were identified as 
students with special education programming needs at the time of registration with. None of the 
newly registered students required programming and services at an out-of-district special education 
school program. 
 
 
b. To discuss the request for a bid waiver to Varsity Brands Holding (BSN Sports) 
 
 
Commissioner Mace made a motion seconded by Commissioner Massarelli  
 
“To approve a bid waiver to Varsity Brands Holding (BSN Sports) for replacement of high school 
uniforms.” 
 
Jodi Bond clarified this was for $26,589 in uniforms for nine athletic teams at BC/BE for both boys and 
girls various sports. Nancy Haynes explained the bidding process, as there are several ways to 
purchase goods and services, and anything over $25,000 is required to go out to bid unless there is an 
existing contract, state contract, CREC, CRCOG, or Sourcewell, contract in place which mirror the 
City’s process. There is a state contract for athletic equipment, uniforms and supplies, which was 
suggested that BOE use. The state contract is readily available, with no need to go out to bid. Chair
August 25, 2026 
Board of Finance Minutes 
 
 
Maikowski questioned if the state contract counts as a bid, and Nancy stated it did not. Jodi Bond 
explained Cera Galluzzo, the Athletic Director, was working with the vendor once the funding was in 
place in the new budget for these teams whose uniforms were up for replacement back in June/July 
as she would be going out on maternity leave. The order was placed, and she didn’t know at the time 
they were no longer on state contract. As soon as they found out BSN was not on state contract, they 
did not order any additional items. The Athletic Director is aware for other uniforms, it needs to go 
out to bid or use state contract.  
 
Commissioner O’Brien asked Nancy to review with the Purchasing Committee trends over the past 
year, contracting requirements, why a bid waiver is needed, and if there are any other Departments 
that try to circumvent the necessary requirements.  
 
 
Following a voice vote in which there was no opposition, the Chairperson declared the motion 
carried.

Commissioner Mace made a motion seconded by Commissioner Campion 
 
“To transfer of $59,800 from the EBSF Contingency account to purchase timeclocks and to 
recommend approval of this action to a Joint Meeting of the City Council and Board of Finance.” 
 
Commissioner Peterson questioned the useful life of these clocks. Commissioner Mace stated they 
were in a similar situation at his work and needed to replace the UKG clocks as they will no 
longer communicate with the system. Diane confirmed the current clocks are 10 years old, and the 
City was just notified otherwise, the items would have been requested to include in the FY27 
budgeted for replacement.
August 25, 2026
